repositories.name: platform-contracts
repositories.reason: Source of truth for the event schemas and OpenAPI specs that gain additive fields (column tags, column classification, masked_columns) and one new metadata-service endpoint; needs a 2.4.0 minor release.

repositories.name: platform-sdk
repositories.reason: Its explicit dataclasses drop undeclared fields, so Column needs classification/tags, Decision needs masked_columns, MetadataClient needs a set-classification method, and the bundled platform-contracts pin must move to 2.4.0 (release 3.5.0).

repositories.name: ingestion-service
repositories.reason: The Postgres connector already reads column_comment (e.g. 'tags: pii,email') but drops it; it must parse the tags and publish them per column on ingestion.schema.discovered.v1 (AC1).

repositories.name: metadata-service
repositories.reason: Owning team: store classification per column, suggest it from ingested tags, preserve steward overrides across re-discovery, expose it on GET columns and a new steward PUT endpoint, and include it in metadata.dataset.changed.v1 (AC1, AC2).

repositories.name: entitlements-service
repositories.reason: Access decisions must return masked_columns (columns classified PII when the principal lacks the pii:read grant), which requires reading column classifications from metadata-service and caching them (AC3).

repositories.name: consumption-gateway
repositories.reason: Entitlements only decides and enforcement happens in the caller, so the gateway must mask the decision's masked_columns in returned rows (AC4).

repositories.name: transformation-service
repositories.reason: Rule selection is by data_type only; it must bind new PII-format rules to columns classified PII, using classification/tags from MetadataClient.get_columns (AC5).

repositories.name: search-indexer
repositories.reason: It validates metadata.dataset.changed.v1 against a vendored 2.1.0 schema with additionalProperties:false at every level, so any new column field would send every event to search-indexer.dlq; the vendored schema must be updated and deployed before metadata-service emits classification (AC6).

repositories.name: platform-e2e
repositories.reason: Cross-service changes require new/updated suites: tags-to-classification ingest flow, masked query for principals without pii:read, and PII transformation rules (team rule in the README).

repositories.name: lineage-service
repositories.reason: Consumes metadata.dataset.changed.v1 as a tolerant reader (urn and name only), so the additive column field should be ignored; re-run tests after the platform-sdk bump.

repositories.name: notification-service
repositories.reason: Consumes transformation.result.published.v1 scores; new PII rules can lower scores and trigger more below-threshold emails, and it uses MetadataClient so it should be re-verified on platform-sdk 3.5.0.

repositories.name: reporting-service
repositories.reason: Listed in the metadata-service README as a consumer of metadata.dataset.changed.v1 but not present in the workspace, so its schema tolerance to the new column field is unknown and must be confirmed with its owners.

considered_not_impacted.name: usage-metering
considered_not_impacted.reason: Consumes only consumption.access.logged.v1 (principal, dataset_urn, row_count), which this plan leaves unchanged, and does not use platform-sdk.

dependencies.contract: platform-contracts (pinned ==2.3.0, bundled schemas used by events.publish validation)

contracts.name: ingestion.schema.discovered.v1
contracts.description: Add optional columns[].tags (array of lowercase strings parsed from the source column comment, e.g. ['pii','email']); schema lives in platform-contracts 2.4.0.

contracts.name: metadata.dataset.changed.v1
contracts.description: Add optional columns[].classification (enum PUBLIC|INTERNAL|CONFIDENTIAL|PII, nullable) and optional columns[].tags; classification overrides are emitted with the existing change_type COLUMNS_CHANGED (no new enum value). Additive per platform-contracts semver, but breaking for search-indexer's strict vendored schema until it is updated.

contracts.name: GET /v1/datasets/{urn}/columns
contracts.description: Column schema gains optional classification (nullable enum), classification_source (SUGGESTED|STEWARD, nullable) and tags (array of strings).

contracts.name: PUT /v1/datasets/{urn}/columns/{column}/classification
contracts.description: Steward sets or overrides a column classification: body {classification, reason?}; returns the updated Column; 404 for unknown dataset/column, 400 for invalid value; publishes metadata.dataset.changed.v1 (COLUMNS_CHANGED).

contracts.name: POST /v1/access/decide
contracts.description: Decision response gains masked_columns (array of column names, empty when the principal holds pii:read or the dataset has no PII columns); request body unchanged; spec version 1.2.0 -> 1.3.0.

contracts.name: POST /v1/query
contracts.description: Values of masked columns in rows are replaced by a mask value, and the 200 response gains an optional masked_columns array so consumers can tell masked from real values; spec version 2.0.0 -> 2.1.0.

open_questions: Is the pii:read grant global, or should it also be scoped (e.g. domain:<domain>:pii:read, dataset:<urn>:pii:read) like existing grants? The plan assumes a literal global 'pii:read' grant, with scoped forms as a follow-up.
Should a SUGGESTED (not steward-confirmed) PII classification be enforced for masking immediately? The plan assumes yes (fail closed).

Mask representation in query results: null, a fixed token such as '****', or a type-preserving value? The plan assumes '****' for string columns and null otherwise, plus the masked_columns response field.

consumption-gateway runs free-form SQL; aliased or derived columns (e.g. select email as e, lower(email)) cannot be masked by result-column name. Is column-name masking acceptable for v1, or must the gateway rewrite/parse SQL or use warehouse-native masking?
Are there other paths to the data (direct warehouse access, exports, notebooks bypassing consumption-gateway) that also need masking?
Who is allowed to call the new classification PUT endpoint (steward role) and how is it authenticated? No auth is visible in metadata-service.
Which tag-to-classification mapping should be used (e.g. pii -> PII, confidential -> CONFIDENTIAL, internal -> INTERNAL, public -> PUBLIC, otherwise no suggestion), and where is it configured?
PII-format rules need a PII subtype (email, phone, ssn, ...). The plan assumes it comes from the source tags (e.g. 'pii,email'); is a dedicated pii_type field preferred?
What should unclassified columns default to (null vs INTERNAL), and is a backfill of existing datasets required before go-live?
Who owns reporting-service (named in the metadata-service README but not in this workspace), and does it validate metadata.dataset.changed.v1 strictly like search-indexer?
Should search-indexer index classification (e.g. a catalog facet) or only accept and ignore it? The plan only accepts it.
Should consumption.access.logged.v1 record which columns were masked for audit? Left unchanged here to avoid touching usage-metering.
transformation results must not include raw failing PII values; confirm the result payload stays limited to column/rule/passed.
